kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea remains paused following episode 56 fountaining on November 5. Summit inflation stalled just before midnight moving the episode 57 forecast window to November 22-26.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: Summit tilt changed from slowly inflating to flat at around 11:30 pm on the night of November 20. Continuous glow remained visible overnight from both the north and southwest vents. Another fountaining episode remains likely and the current forecast window for episode 57 fountaining is November 22-26. Summit Observations: Summit webcams recorded strong to moderate glow from both the north and southwest vents overnight. Views from the V1cam livestream webcam overnight showed nearly continuous flames and minor spattering from the north and southwest vents. A helicopter overflight on November 18 confirmed the presence of a large lava pond within the southwest vent that occasionally was spattering and overturning. The north vent was largely crusted over but had two pukas (holes) that are the source of the flames and spatter visible at night. Seismic tremor remained continuous over the past day. No earthquakes were located beneath the summit in the past day. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) has recorded nearly continuous summit inflation since the end of episode 56 lava fountaining. Tilt had been slowly inflating since the afternoon of November 19, but became flat to slightly deflationary around 11:30 pm on November 20. This morning, UWD had regained about 0.5 microradians of tilt during the past day, before flattening out, resulting in a total of about 14.7 microradians of inflationary tilt since the end of episode 56. The average sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate could not be accurately measured yesterday, November 20, due to dynamic wind conditions. Trade winds this morning are carrying volcanic gases to the southwest. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following the end of episode 56 on November 5, 2026, summit tiltmeters have recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with nearly continuous inflationary tilt at UWD. Tiltmeters showed inflationary tilt being recorded on the UWD tiltmeter since the afternoon of November 19, which became flat to slightly deflationary at about 11:30 pm on November 20 and continues this morning. Modelling based on ongoing tilt trends, along with glow and minor spatter seen within the eruptive vents, all indicate another fountaining episode is likely. The forecast window for episode 57 fountaining is November 22-26. Changes from inflation to deflation at the summit can result in the dates of the forecast window being extended. If inflation remains stalled for a while or slow inflation rates return, then episode 57 is most likely to start during the latter part of the forecast window. If inflation rate increases, then episode 57 could start earlier in the forecast window. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Summary of episode 56: Lava fountaining occurred between 12:10 p.m. and 6:01 p.m. on November 5, 2026. Maximum fountain heights were about 660 feet (200 meters). Only the north vent produced fountaining. Tephra fallout was primarily towards the southwest, in closed areas of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park, with trace amounts on Highway 11. The eruptive plume rose as high as 18,000 feet (5,500 meters) above sea level. Tiltmeter data indicate approximately 8 million cubic yards (6 million cubic meters) of lava were erupted, with an average eruption rate of 260 cubic yards (200 cubic meters) per second. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
